findings.title: Collision-case remedy `cf config unset … --project` deletes the personal value, not the stale shared copy
findings.description:
The design routes `delete` by the key's scope (line 89), and `migrate-personal` is named "the one exception" that touches the other file.
- For `git.integration_branch`, a personal key, `cf config unset git.integration_branch --project` deletes it from `.context-forge.local.toml`. That is the code path `ConfigManager.delete` takes at `ConfigManager.ts:187-204` once routing is added.
- The `skipped (personal value already set)` message (line 146) and walkthrough step 9 (line 259) both give this command as the way to clear the stale shared copy.
- Run as written, step 9 destroys the developer's personal `legacy/value` and leaves the stale shared value in place. Reads then fall back to the stale value, and `cf check` still warns.
- The design needs a real way to remove a personal key from the shared file. Options are a `migrate-personal --force` or `--discard` flag, or an `unset` behavior for stale shared copies. Walkthrough step 9 must then be rewritten and run against the real behavior.

findings.title: No API for reading or moving keys across files; "signatures unchanged" and "helpers reused as-is" don't hold
findings.description:
`migrate-personal` and the checker rule both need raw access to the shared file's personal keys.
- `get`/`set`/`delete` all route by key scope. Through the public API, `migrate-personal` cannot read a personal key from the shared file: `get` returns the personal value or the fallback with no source split. It also cannot delete from the shared file.
- `readToml`, `writeToml`, `resolveKey` and `deleteKey` are module-private in `ConfigManager.ts:21-89`. The design says they are "reused as-is", but nothing outside that module can call them.
- `ConsistencyChecker` has only an optional `ConfigManager` (`ConsistencyChecker.ts:45-48`, imported type-only at line 21) and `project.projectPath`. It has no way to enumerate raw shared-file keys.
- The design therefore needs new `ConfigManager` public methods, for example `listPersonalKeysInSharedFile()`, `moveToPersonal(key)` or an exported TOML helper module. These must be specified: the contract, the return shape, and the `config === undefined` case.
- Line 49 ("signatures are unchanged… no changes beyond Technical Scope") and line 153 ("Consumers to update: none") are inaccurate.
- `ConsistencyChecker.ts` imports `fs` directly in places, so raw reads in the checker are possible. The design must still pick a mechanism and say which.

findings.title: `cf init` gitignore step placement is unspecified and conflicts with the existing `init` flow
findings.description:
The walkthrough runs `cf init --lite` (line 227) and then expects `.gitignore` to contain the entry (line 239).
- In `init.ts:85-117`, everything outside project registration is gated by `if (!opts.lite)`. The design does not say the gitignore step sits outside that gate.
- The early return for a worktree of a registered project (`init.ts:71-74`) skips any later step.
- Existing installations are not covered. `cf init` is the only place the ignore line is added. A user who upgrades and runs `cf config set git.integration_branch X --project` gets an untracked, un-ignored `.context-forge.local.toml` unless they happen to re-run `cf init`. That recreates the leak the slice exists to prevent.
- The detection rule only flags personal keys in the shared file. It does not flag a non-ignored local file.
- Either have the first write to the personal file ensure the ignore entry, or add a `cf check` finding for it. The design should also state which directory's `.gitignore` is used when `projectPath` is not the git root.

findings.title: Checker rule scope and surfacing claim are not verified against `check()` vs `checkAll()`
findings.description:
The design says the finding "surfaces automatically through `cf check` and MCP `workflow_check`, since both already run the full suite".
- `check()` returns an empty result when no active slice is set (`ConsistencyChecker.ts:59-62`). `cf check --slice N` (`check.ts:217-222`) uses `check()`.
- The rule is project-level, so it belongs only in `checkAll()`. The design does not say so.
- `cf check` merges results across worktree views and dedupes (`check.ts:207-213`). Because the rule reads one project-level file, the "exactly one warning" criterion (line 217) depends on that dedup. This should be stated.
- The design claims the rule goes in "alongside the existing config-hygiene-style checks". No such checks exist in the file. The only config usage is `resolveGateConfig`.
- The rule also runs only when `this.config` is present, since the checker's config is optional. The no-config case needs a statement.

findings.title: Failure handling for a malformed or unreadable personal file is not enumerated, and `branchGuard` degrades silently
findings.description:
The failure-modes section covers write failures and `migrate-personal`, but not read failures on the new file.
- `readToml` rethrows everything except ENOENT, so a hand-edited, corrupt `.context-forge.local.toml` now makes `get('git.integration_branch')` throw.
- `branchGuard.evaluateBranchGuard` catches all `get` errors and silently falls back to `trunk = 'main'` (`branchGuard.ts:83-95`). A corrupt personal file would therefore quietly disable the integration-branch guard (916), which exists specifically to protect `main`. The design should say whether that is acceptable or whether the guard should surface the error.
- Since the guard's whole purpose is protecting `main`, this deserves an explicit decision.

findings.title: MCP `config_get` surface change is mis-described and the tool descriptions go stale
findings.description:
The design says `config_get` "response includes both project config paths".
- `configPaths` is returned only in the list branch (key omitted), at `configTools.ts:36-43`. The keyed branch returns only the `ConfigResult`.
- The design should say whether the new `source: 'project-personal'` on the keyed branch is enough there.
- The `config_get` description says "Resolution order: project config → user config → default" (`configTools.ts:15`). The `config_set` description (lines 56-58) also needs updating, since personal-key writes now go to a different file. Neither is listed.
- The design does not list the `configPaths` response key. A new key such as `projectPersonal` has to be named.
- `mcp-server/tests/configTools.test.ts:14-22` mocks `@context-forge/core/node` with only `getProjectConfigPath`. The new helper must be added to that mock and exported through `config/index.ts` and `node.ts`. This is a minor fixture update. The "fixture updates only" statement should name it.

findings.title: `migrate-personal` option shape and command registration are inconsistent with the existing `config` surface
findings.description: The design specifies `-p, --project <id>` (required value). Every other `config` subcommand uses `-p, --project [id]`, with a bare flag meaning "resolve from CWD" (`config.ts:68, 110, 140`). Walkthrough step 6 and Technical Scope also refer to the CLI surface as unchanged. The design should reuse `resolveConfigProjectPath` and `resolveScopeAndPath`, with the same optional-value semantics. It should also state that `--global` is not accepted. The parent command description `(get, set, unset)` at `config.ts:64` is not mentioned for update.

findings.title: Proportionality: several mechanisms exceed what the slice needs
findings.description:
- The three-way collision matrix (absent, identical, different), the `failed: <error>` per-key reporting and the idempotency argument form a large migration spec for a single personal key, `git.integration_branch`. The registry has exactly one personal key. The per-key independent processing and partial-failure reporting could be cut to a plain loop that stops on the first error. Because the order is write-then-delete, that is already safe and re-runnable.
- The design restates the decision rationale for the `.local.` naming and the rejected `[personal]` table at length. The "Integration Points" and "Risk Assessment" sections largely restate earlier sections.
- Three of the Technical Requirements restate "no `any`" and "existing tests pass". Trim these.
- The design is otherwise within what the plan assigns. The detection rule and `migrate-personal` are both required by plan entry 915's migration/compat requirement, so those should not be deferred.

findings.title: Rationale says "per-worktree" but the personal file is per-project-root
findings.description: `ConfigManager` is constructed with the registered `project.projectPath` (`guides.ts:46, 52`, `check.ts:185`). That is the main checkout, not the worktree directory. The personal file is therefore shared across all worktrees of a project, not per-worktree as line 111 states. Per-worktree integration branches would need per-worktree personal files, which this design does not provide. Correct the rationale, or state that this is intentional.

findings.title: Verified claims
findings.description:
- The `ConfigResult.source` consumers at `config.ts:86, 100` interpolate the value as a plain string, as claimed.
- `fixAction.type` is the closed union `'update-checkbox' | 'update-frontmatter'` (`types.ts:240`), as claimed.
- `CONFIG_KEYS` contains 15 keys, matching the classification table once the four `workflow.review_gates.*.threshold` keys are counted. The table's `workflow.review_gates.*.threshold` wildcard row is acceptable. The registry is typed `Record<string, ConfigKeyDefinition>`, so a missing `scope` is caught by the compiler only on the object literals.
- No other code reads `.context-forge.toml` directly. Only `ConfigManager` and `configTools.ts` use the path helper.
- `cf init` writes no `.gitignore` today, as claimed.
